summary: Walker County, GA: CCC wooden tower 1940, steel tower 1961, dismantled 1979; an overlook platform now sits on the site, reached by an unpaved road.

facts.design: 1940 CCC wooden tower, 60 ft with 8x8 ft cab and catwalk; 1961 steel tower, 80 ft with 6x6 ft metal cab
facts.status_note: Steel tower dismantled in 1979; an overlook platform stands on the former tower site
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Chattahoochee National Forest

access.note: Road runs up to the overlook from Pocket Road, about four miles along it from the Villanow crossroads; the road is unpaved

events.note: Built by the Civilian Conservation Corps at a Civil War Confederate signal flagpole site; wooden tower 60 ft
Wooden tower torn down by the Forest Service; steel tower put up close by
Overlook platform built by the Accelerated Public Works Program on the former tower site
Steel tower dismantled and donated to the Walker County Correctional Institute
Area officially became a recreation area, developed by the Youth Conservation Corps

corrections.proposed: 1940 built by the CCC (wooden tower); 1979 removed (steel tower dismantled)
corrections.why: The OSM start_date 1979-09-25 is a map-node date. Both local histories date the first tower to 1940 and give 1979 as the year the steel tower was dismantled.
18.3 m (60 ft) is the 1940 wooden tower, torn down in 1961. The steel tower that stood until 1979 was 80 ft, about 24.4 m.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: OSM gives 1979-09-25 as a start date. The local histories say the wooden tower was built in 1940 and the steel tower was removed in 1979. The story follows the histories and says so.
Sources give 60 ft for the 1940 wooden tower and 80 ft for the 1961 to 1979 steel tower. The facts record the steel tower, the last one standing, and the design text gives both.

notes_for_editor: 1940 and 1961 build dates, the 60 ft and 80 ft heights and the 1979 removal all come from the Armuchee Ranger District history as quoted on the Eastern US lookouts page; the Villanow blog agrees on the dates. No official Forest Service, NHLR or FFLOS record was read. Staffing and fires: no source found, so omitted. The overlook platform is the only present feature described, and no source says whether tower footings remain. Access and drive-up come from the blog, so check the current road before any claim about present access. The brief's 1979 build date came from the OSM start_date and is corrected.
